source_text:
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate.
Abundantia peccatorum solet fratres conturbare.
propter hoc dominus noster uoluit nos praemonere
comparans regnum caelorum reticulo misso in mare
congreganti multos pisces omne genus hinc et inde.
quos cum traxissent ad litus, tunc coeperunt separare,
bonos in uasa miserunt, reliquos malos in mare.
quisquis nouit euangelium, recognoscat cum timore.
uidet reticulum ecclesiam, uidet hoc saeculum mare;
genus autem mixtum piscis iustus est cum peccatore;
saeculi finis est litus: tunc est tempus separare;
qui modo retia ruperunt, multum dilexerunt mare;
uasa sunt sedes sanctorum, quo non possunt peruenire.
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate.
Bonus auditor fortasse quaerit, qui ruperint rete.
homines multum superbi, qui iustos se dicunt esse.
sic fecerunt (et) scissuram et altare contra altare.
diabolo se tradiderunt, cum pugnant de traditione
et crimen quod commiserunt in alios uolunt transferre.
ipsi tradiderunt libros et nos audent accusare,
ut peius committant scelus quam commiserunt et ante.
qui possent causam librorum excusare de timore,
quia Petrus Christum negauit, dum terreretur de morte,
modo quo pacto excusabunt factum altare contra altare
et pace Christi conscissa spem reponunt in homine?
quod persecutio non fecit, ipsi fecerunt in pace.
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate.
Custos noster, deus magne, tu nos potes liberare
a pseudoprophetis istis, qui nos quaerunt deuorare.
maledictum cor lupinum contegunt ouina pelle.
nomen iusti ouina pellis, schisma est in lupino corde.
qui non nouerunt scripturas, hos solent circumuenire;
audiunt enim \'traditores\' et nesciunt quid gestum est ante.
quibus si dicam: \'probate\', non habent quid respondere.
suis se dicunt credidisse: dico ego mentitos esse;
quia et nos credidimus nostris, qui eos dicunt tradidisse.
uis nosse qui dicant falsum? qui non sunt in unitate.
olim iam causa finita est, quod uos non statis in pace.
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate.
Dixerunt maiores nostri et libros fecerunt inde,
qui tunc causam cognouerunt, quo recens possent probare:
erant quidam traditores librorum de sancta lege
episcopi de Numidia et non quilibet de plebe.
cum Carthaginem uenissent episcopum ordinare,
inuenerunt Caecilianum iam ordinatum in sua sede.
irati sunt, quia ipsi non potuerunt ordinare.
erant Botrus et Caelestius hostes Caeciliano ualde,
impii fures superbi, de quibus longum est referre.
iunxerunt se simul omnes crimen in illum conflare,
dicunt ordinatorem eius sanctos libros tradidisse.
sic pacis retia ruperunt et errant modo per mare.
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate.
Ecce quam bonum et iocundum fratres in unum habitare!!
audite uocem prophetae, ut sitis in unitate.
crimen nobis quis probauit antiquum de traditione?
quis obiecit in iudicio? qui sederunt iudicare?
quibus testibus conuicit, quis ausus est affirmare?
sed hoc libenter finxerunt, quod se nouerant fecisse.
quia fama iam loquebatur de librorum traditione,
sed qui fecerant latebant in illa perturbatione,
inde alios infamarunt, ut se ipsos possent celare.
per illos ceteri errarunt principes ex ipsa parte,
quia non credere collegis putauerunt sibi turpe.
iam, fratres, finiatur error et simus in unitate.
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate.
Fecerunt quod uoluerunt tunc in illa caecitate.
non iudices consederunt, non sacerdotes de more,
quo solent in magnis causis congregati iudicare,
non accusator et reus steterunt in quaestione,
non testis, non documentum, quo possent crimen probare,
sed furor dolus tumultus, qui regnant in falsitate.
proferantur nobis gesta, quae in concilio solent esse,
uideamus quae res coegit fieri altare contra altare.
si malus erat sacerdos, deponendus erat ante,
si non poterat deponi, tolerandus intra rete,
sicut modo toleratis tam multos malos aperte,
et qui fertis pio furore, ferretis unum pro pace.
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate.
Gaudium magnum esset nobis, si tunc nolletis errare;
sed si tunc non uisum est uerum, uel nunc experti uidete.
multos nunc habetis prauos, qui uobis displicent ualde,
nec tamen hos separatis a uestra communione.
non dico de illis peccatis, quae potestis et negare:
fustes ignes mortes dico, quae committunt uestri in luce,
et tamen suffertis illos uel errore uel timore.
quantum erat, ferrent unum patres uestri pro unitate,
si tantus erat tumultus, ut non possent degradare.
adde quod innocens erat et nil poterant probare.
sed ne crimen quaereretur, ubi se uidebant esse,
finxerunt se nimis iustos, cum totum uellent turbare.
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate.
Honores uanos qui quaerit, non uult cum Christo regnare,
sicut princeps huius mali, de cuius uocantur parte.
nam Donatus tunc uolebat Africam totam obtinere;
tunc iudices transmarinos petiit ab imperatore.
sed haec tam iusta petitio non erat de caritate.
hoc ipsa ueritas clamat, quam uolo modo referre.
nam consensit imperator, misit qui sederent Romae
sacerdotes, qui tunc possent Caecilianum cum illo audire.
dicta causa est, nil probatum est: ausus est et appellare
et post collegarum sedem audiri ab imperatore.
hinc petitio illa probatur non esse de caritate.
deinde ubique uictus coepit christianos rebaptizare.
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate.
Iustitiam sequi si uultis, totam causam cogitate.
quod postea fecit Donatus, factum quare non est ante?
dissentiebant sacerdotes in tota Africana parte:
sacerdotes transmarini possent inde iudicare.
quid cucurristis ad schisma et altare contra altare,
ut, quod postea iudicatum est, iam non possetis audire
et a iudicibus uestris cogeremini appellare,
dum uultis erroris regnum quoquo modo confirmare?
et nunc et uos totum noscitis, sed fingitis uos nescire,
et cum uos ueritas urget, patres dicitis errasse,
quasi uos aliquis uetet iam recedere ab errore.
sed superbia uos ligauit in cathedra pestilentiae.
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate.
Karitatem Christi qui habet, pacem non potest odisse.
uel uos iam, populi, audite et nobiscum concordate,
qui non tenetis cathedram, pro qua pugnetis iniuste.
si modo episcopi uestri ex una aliqua regione
haberent inter se litem, quos uelletis iudicare
nisi alterarum regionum qui non essent de ipsa lite?
sed cum discussissent causam, pronuntiarent pro una parte,
numquam communicaretis qui illis nollent consentire.
quare ergo communicastis istis, qui hoc fecerunt ante?
nam et ipsi non consenserunt transmarinorum sententiae,
qui pro nobis iudicarunt; nam nobis iunguntur hodie.
si iudex Christus hoc dicat, quid habetis respondere?
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate.
Lumen cordis si est in uobis, uerum potestis uidere.
sunt preces Donati et acta, quibus quod dictum est probate.
quae si credere non uultis, uos huc aliqua proferte.
quibus si et nos non credimus, erit rixa sine fine.
amplectamur ergo pacem. quid ad nos quod gestum est ante?
obicitis traditionem: respondemus uos fecisse.
clamatis uos de Macario: et nos de circumcellione.
illud nostrum iam transactum: uestri non cessant usque hodie.
habet paleas area nostra: uos hoc solum uultis esse;
uos enim non uultis pacem. illi minantur de fuste:
et utinam minarentur et non tunderent cotidie.
hos si expellunt isti uestri, non habent per quos regnare.
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate.
Modum si excessit Macarius conscriptum in christiana lege,
uel legem regis referebat, ut pugnaret pro unitate.
non dico istum nil peccasse, sed uestros peiores esse.
quis enim praecepit illis per Africam sic saeuire?
non Christus, non imperator haec probatur permisisse,
fustes et ignes priuatos et insaniam sine lege.
quia scriptum est: reconde gladium, scelus non putant in fuste,
non ut homo moriatur, sed ut conquassetur ualde
et postea moriatur inde, iam cruciatus languore.
sed tamen si miserentur, occidunt et uno fuste.
fustes Israheles uocant, quod dixerunt cum honore,
ut plus uastent ipsum nomen quam corpus quod caedunt inde.
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate.
Nolite nobis iam, fratres, tempus Macarii imputare.
si crudeles erant illi, et nobis displicent ualde;
si autem falsa de illis dicunt, deus potest iudicare.
nos amemus pacem Christi, gaudeamus in unitate.
si qui sunt mali in ecclesia, nil nobis possunt nocere.
si non possunt nobiscum esse, excludantur salua pace.
si non poterunt excludi, excludantur uel de corde.
dixit Ezechiel sanctus quosdam consignatos esse,
qui gemunt peccata fratrum et non se separant inde.
sic nos propter malos fratres non separemur a matre,
quod tunc impii fecerunt extra leuantes altare,
ut peiores nunc haberent quam quos se fingunt fugisse.
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate.
Omnis qui scripturas legit nouit quod uolo aperire.
Iohannes Baptista dixit tunc ad Iudaeos aperte,
quod illos tamquam aream suam posset Christus uentilare.
misit in messem operarios discipulos praedicare,
per quos area collecta est et uentilata de cruce.
tunc iusti tamquam frumentum ecclesias implerunt caste
uendentes quae possidebant et mundo dicentes uale.
illi tamquam semen erant, quod toto dispersum est orbe,
ut alia surgeret messis, quae uentilanda est in fine.
haec crescit inter zizania, quia sunt haereses ubique;
huius palea sunt iniusti, qui non sunt in unitate.
ex quibus si erat Macarius, nos quid uis rebaptizare?
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate.
Pone in corde areas duas, ut possis quod dico uidere.
certe et priores habebant sanctos, sicut ostendunt scripturae.
185 nam et septem milia uirorum deus se dixit reliquisse,
et sacerdotes et reges multi iusti sunt in lege.
ibi habes tantos prophetas, habes multos et de plebe.
dic mihi quis tunc iustorum separauit sibi altare.
multa scelera admittebat iniquus populus ille,
idolis sacrificatum est, tot occisi sunt prophetae
et nemo tamen iustorum recessit ab unitate.
iusti iniustos sufferebant uenturo uentilatore,
uno templo miscebantur, sed mixti non erant corde,
dicebant in illos tanta et unum habebant altare.
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate.
Quid uobis ad haec uidetur? secunda messis ecclesiae,
quae per totum orbem crescit, plura debet sustinere:
habet [et]iam domini exemplum et in Iuda traditore.
hunc inter bonos ferebat, hunc misit et praedicare.
malus seruus praedicabat, sed Christus erat in fide,
quia qui iudici credebant non curabant de praecone.
quando dedit sanctam cenam, nec tunc illum exclusit inde,
et posset per illum tradi, etiam si inde exisset ante.
sed nobis exemplum datum est malos fratres tolerare,
ut, cum non possunt excludi, solo separemur corde.
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate.
Rogo, respondete nobis, quid uultis rebaptizare.
lapsos sacerdotes uestros pellitis a communione
et nemo tamen post illos ausus est rebaptizare
et quoscumque baptizarunt uobis communicant hodie.
quid ab eis acceperunt, si non habebant quid dare?
legite quomodo adulteri puniantur in sancta lege;
non enim dicere possunt, quia peccarunt a timore.
si sancti soli baptizant, post istos rebaptizate.
quid calumniamini nobis, quia sumus in unitate,
qui nondum eramus nati in illa persecutione?.
scriptum est peccata patrum ad filios non pertinere,
sed nemo dat fructum bonum, si praecisus est de uite.
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate.
Scitis catholica quid sit et quid sit praecisum a uite.
si qui sunt inter uos cauti, ueniant, uiuant in radice;
antequam nimis arescant, iam liberentur ab igne.
ideo non rebaptizamus, quod unum signum est in fide,
non quia uos sanctos uidemus, sed solam formam tenere,
quia ipsam formam habet sarmentum, quod praecisum est de uite.
sed quid illi prodest forma, si non uiuit de radice?
uenite, fratres, si uultis, ut inseramini in uite.
dolor est cum uos uidemus praecisos ita iacere.
numerate sacerdotes uel ab ipsa Petri sede
et in ordine illo patrum quis cui successit uidete:
ipsa est petra quam non uincunt superbae inferorum portae.
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate..
Talis si quis ad te ueniat plenus catholica fide,
quales illos sanctos uiros omnes solemus audire,
et si tibi dicat: \'frater, quid me uis rebaptizare?
quid sit ante factum nescio, nunc autem sum in Christi fide.
si me maculat quod nescio, tu qualis sis nunc ostende:
uultus tuos ecce attendo, ignoro quid sit in corde.
si me maculat quod nescio, tu me maculas fortasse,
et si te credo esse sanctum, quibus communicas uide.
si maculat quod nescimus, iam non potes sanctus esse,
quem maculant tot peccata, quae committunt uestri occulte.
si autem quod nescis non curas, nec ego quod factum est ante*. —
et tamen christianum talem audes <tu) rebaptizare.
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate.
Uae qui pro cathedris uestris sic contenditis iniuste.
clamatis uos solos sanctos, aliud dicitis in corde,
quia uidetis et uos multos malos abundare ubique.
numquid dicere potestis: \'mixti sumus intra rete\'?
respondetur enim uobis iam uos illud disrupisse.
neque dicere potestis paleas uos sustinere;
iterum enim respondemus: hoc fecissetis et ante.
non enim peiores erant illo Iuda traditore,
cum quo apostoli acceperunt primum sacramentum cenae,
cum tanti sceleris reum inter se iam scirent esse;
nec tamen hos inquinabant sordes in alieno corde.
et tamen christianos fratres audetis rebaptizare.
Omnes qui gaudetis de pace, modo uerum iudicate.
Audite, fratres, quod dico, et mihi irasci nolite.
quia non sunt falsa quae auditis, potestis et considerare.
quid si ipsa mater ecclesia uos alloquatur cum pace
et dicat: \'o filii mei, quid querimini de matre?
quare me deseruistis, iam uolo a uobis audire.
accusatis fratres uestros et ego laceror ualde.
quando me premebant gentes, multa tuli cum dolore.
multi me deseruerunt, sed fecerunt in timore;
uos uero nullus coegit sic contra me rebellare.
dicitis mecum uos esse, sed falsum uidetis esse:
ego catholica dicor et uos de Donati parte.
iussit me apostolus pro regibus mundi orare;
uos inuidetis, quod reges iam sunt in christiana fide.
si filii estis, quid inuidetis, quia auditae sunt preces meae?
quando enim dona miserunt, noluistis acceptare
et obliti estis prophetas, qui illud praedixerunt ante,
quod gentium reges magni missuri essent dona ecclesiae.
quae dona cum respuistis, ostendistis uos non esse
et Macarium coegistis suum dolorem uindicare.
sed ego quid uobis feci, uestra mater in toto orbe?
expello malos quos possum, quos non possum cogor ferre;
fero illos, donec sanentur aut separentur in fine.
uos me quare dimisistis et crucior de uestra morte?
si multum malos odistis, quales habetis uidete.
si et uos toleratis malos, quare non in unitate,
ubi nemo rebaptizat nec altare est contra altare?
malos tantos toleratis, sed nulla bona mercede,
quia, quod debetis pro Christo, pro Donato uultis ferre\'.
cantauimus uobis, fratres, pacem, si uultis audire.
uenturus est iudex noster: nos damus, exigit ille.
orientation: Augustine opens his psalm by addressing all who rejoice in peace, urging them to judge the Donatist controversy truly, and begins retelling the origin of the schism.
pass_a_gloss:
All [you] who rejoice of peace, now [the] truth judge. Abundance of sins is accustomed brothers to disturb. because of this our Lord willed us to forewarn comparing [the] kingdom of heavens to [a] net sent into [the] sea gathering many fish [of] every kind from here and from there. whom when they had dragged to [the] shore, then they began to separate, [the] good into vessels they sent, [the] remaining bad into [the] sea. whoever knows [the] gospel, let him recognize with fear. he sees [the] net [to be the] church, he sees this world [to be the] sea; [the] kind however mixed [of] fish is [the] just [one] with [the] sinner; [the] end [of the] world is [the] shore: then is [the] time to separate; [those] who now [the] nets tore, much loved [the] sea; [the] vessels are [the] seats [of the] saints, where they cannot arrive. All [you] who rejoice of peace, now [the] truth judge. [A] good hearer perhaps asks, who tore [the] net. men much proud, who themselves just say to be. thus they made [both] [a] tear and [an] altar against [an] altar. to [the] devil themselves they handed over, when they fight about tradition and [the] crime which they committed onto others they wish to transfer. themselves they handed over [the] books and us they dare to accuse, so that [a] worse crime they commit than [they] committed also before. [they] who could [the] case [of the] books excuse from fear, because Peter Christ denied, while he was terrified of death, now by what pact will they excuse [the] deed [of] altar against altar and [the] peace [of] Christ torn [apart] [their] hope they place in man? what persecution did not do, themselves they did in peace. All [you] who rejoice of peace, now [the] truth judge. [Our] guardian, God great, you us can free from [the] false prophets these, who us seek to devour. [a] cursed heart [of a] wolf they cover [with] sheep's skin. [the] name [of the] just [one is the] sheep's skin, [the] schism is in [the] wolfish heart. [those] who do not know [the] scriptures, these they are accustomed to deceive; they hear for "traitors" and do not know what was done before. to whom if I say: "prove [it]", they do not have what to answer. to their own [people] they say they believed: I say [that] they lied to be; because also we believed our own [people], who them say to have handed over. do you wish to know who say [the] false [thing]? [those] who are not in unity. long ago already [the] case is finished, because you do not stand in peace. All [you] who rejoice of peace, now [the] truth judge. [The] elders our said and books they made from there, [those] who then [the] case knew, where [the] recent [events] they could prove: there were certain traitors [of the] books [of the] holy law bishops of Numidia and not any [ones] of [the] people. when to Carthage they had come [a] bishop to ordain, they found Caecilianus already ordained in his seat. angry they were, because themselves they could not ordain. there were Botrus and Caelestius enemies to Caecilianus greatly, impious thieves proud, of whom [it is] long to report. they joined themselves together all [a] crime against him to forge, they say [the] ordainer his [the] holy books to have handed over. thus [the] nets [of] peace they tore and they wander now through [the] sea. All [you] who rejoice of peace, now [the] truth judge. Behold how good and pleasant [it is for] brothers in one to dwell!! hear [the] voice [of the] prophet, so that you may be in unity. [the] crime to us who proved [the] ancient [one] about tradition? who objected in judgment? [those] who sat to judge? by what witnesses [was he] convicted, who dared to affirm? but this willingly they invented, because themselves they knew to have done [it]. because [the] report already was speaking about [the] tradition [of the] books, but [those] who had done [it] were hiding in that disturbance, from there others they defamed, so that themselves they could hide. through those [the] rest erred [the] leaders from that very side, because not to believe [their] colleagues they thought to themselves [to be] shameful. now, brothers, let [the] error be ended and let us be in unity. All [you] who rejoice of peace, now [the] truth judge. They did what they wanted then in that blindness. not judges sat together, not priests according to custom, in which [way] they are accustomed in great cases gathered to judge, not [the] accuser and [the] accused stood in [the] inquiry, not [a] witness, not [a] document, by which they could [the] crime prove, but fury deceit tumult, which reign in falsehood. let [the] records be brought forth to us, which in [a] council are accustomed to be, let us see what thing compelled [it] to be done [an] altar against [an] altar. if evil was [the] priest, [he was] to be deposed before, if he could not be deposed, [he was] to be tolerated within [the] net, just as now you tolerate so many bad [ones] openly, and [you] who bear [them] with pious fury, you would bear one for peace. All [you] who rejoice of peace, now [the] truth judge. [A] joy great would be to us, if then you were unwilling to err; but if then [it] was not seen [to be] true, at least now [having] experienced [it] see. many now you have depraved [ones], who to you displease greatly, and yet not these you separate from your communion. I do not speak about those sins, which you can also deny: clubs fires deaths I speak [of], which commit your [people] in [the] light, and yet you tolerate them either by error or by fear. how much was [it], your fathers would bear one for unity, if so great was [the] tumult, that they could not degrade [him]. add that innocent he was and nothing they could prove. but lest [the] crime be sought, where themselves they saw to be, they pretended themselves too just, when [the] whole [thing] they wished to disturb. All [you] who rejoice of peace, now [the] truth judge. [The] honors vain [one] who seeks, [he] does not wish with Christ to reign, just as [the] prince [of] this evil, from whose [name] they are called [of the] party. for Donatus then wished Africa [the] whole to obtain; then judges overseas he sought from [the] emperor. but this so just petition was not from charity. this [the] truth itself cries out, which I wish now to report. for [the] emperor consented, [he] sent [those] who should sit at Rome priests, who then could Caecilianus with him hear. [the] case was spoken, nothing was proved: he dared also to appeal and after [the] seat [of the] colleagues to be heard by [the] emperor. from this [the] petition that is proved not to be from charity. then everywhere defeated he began Christians to rebaptize. All [you] who rejoice of peace, now [the] truth judge. Justice to follow if you wish, [the] whole case consider. what afterwards did Donatus, [the] deed why was [it] not before? they disagreed [the] priests in [the] whole African region: [the] priests overseas could from there judge. why did you run to schism and [an] altar against [an] altar, so that, what afterwards was judged, no longer you could hear and by your judges you were compelled to appeal, while you wish [the] kingdom [of] error in any way to confirm? and now also you [the] whole [thing] know, but you pretend yourselves not to know, and when you [the] truth presses, [your] fathers you say to have erred, as if you someone forbids now to withdraw from [the] error. but pride you has bound in [the] chair [of] pestilence.
All [you] who rejoice of peace, now [the] truth judge. [The] charity of Christ [he] who has, peace not can [to] hate. or you now, peoples, hear and with us agree, [you] who not hold [the] chair, for which you fight unjustly. if now [the] bishops of you from one some region had between themselves [a] dispute, whom would you wish [to] judge except [those] of other regions who not were from [the] same dispute? but when they had examined [the] case, they would pronounce for one side, never would you communicate [with those] who to them not wished [to] consent. why therefore have you communicated [with] these, who this did before? for also they not agreed [with the] of [the] overseas [ones] sentence, who for us judged; for to us they are joined today. if [the] judge Christ this says, what have you [to] answer? All [you] who rejoice of peace, now [the] truth judge. [The] light of [the] heart if is in you, [the] truth you can [to] see. are [the] prayers of Donatus and [the] acts, by which what has been said prove. which if [to] believe not you wish, you here some bring forth. choices.why: The glossary requires this exact rendering for the schismatic rival altar.
The glossary requires 'traitors' for those accused of handing over the scriptures.
Renders 'cathedra' as 'seat' here (not 'see') because it refers to the psalm's 'seat of pestilence', not the episcopal see; 'pestilentiae' as 'pestilence'.
Literal rendering of the wolf-in-sheep's-clothing image; 'ouina' is an adjective meaning 'of sheep'.
Literal list of the violent acts attributed to the Donatists' partisans; keeps the plural nouns as bare nouns.
Glossary requires 'see' for cathedra, referring to the episcopal seat of legitimate authority.
Refers to bishops from across the sea who judged the case; 'overseas' is the natural English for transmarinus.
In this context traditio refers to the accusation of handing over the scriptures, i.e., betrayal; 'betrayal' captures the polemical force.
Glossary requires 'circumcellion' for circumcelliones, the violent Donatist partisans.
Glossary requires 'chaff' for palea, representing sinners within the church.
Glossary requires 'unity' for unitas, opposed to Donatist separation.

pass_b_english: All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly. The abundance of sinners often troubles brothers. For this reason our Lord wanted to warn us, comparing the kingdom of heaven to a net cast into the sea, gathering many fish of every kind from here and there. When they had dragged them to the shore, then they began to separate them: the good they put into vessels, the rest, the bad, into the sea. Whoever knows the Gospel should recognize this with fear. He sees the net as the church, he sees this world as the sea; the mixed kind of fish is the righteous person with the sinner; the end of the world is the shore: then is the time to separate. Those who have now broken the nets have loved the sea greatly; the vessels are the seats of the saints, where they cannot arrive.

All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly. A good listener perhaps asks who broke the net. Very proud men, who say they are righteous. They made both a split and altar against altar. They handed themselves over to the devil when they fight about the handing over, and the crime they committed they want to transfer to others. They themselves handed over the books and they dare to accuse us, so that they commit a worse crime than they committed before. They could excuse the matter of the books out of fear, because Peter denied Christ when he was terrified of death. But now how will they excuse the making of altar against altar, and having torn the peace of Christ they place their hope in a human being? What persecution did not do, they did in time of peace.

All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly. Our guardian, great God, you can free us from these false prophets who seek to devour us. They cover a cursed wolf-like heart with a sheep's skin. The name of a righteous person is the sheep's skin; the schism is in the wolf-like heart. Those who do not know the Scriptures, these they usually deceive. For they hear 'traitors' and do not know what happened before. If I say to them, 'Prove it,' they have nothing to answer. They say they believed their own people: I say they have lied. Because we also believed our own people, who say that they handed them over. Do you want to know who speaks falsely? Those who are not in unity. The case was finished long ago; as for you, you do not stand in peace.

All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly. Our ancestors spoke and made books about it, those who then examined the case, so they could prove it while it was fresh: there were certain traitors of the books of the holy law, bishops from Numidia and not just any from the people. When they came to Carthage to ordain a bishop, they found Caecilian already ordained in his see. They were angry because they themselves could not ordain. Botrus and Caelestius were great enemies of Caecilian, impious, proud thieves, about whom it would take long to tell. They all joined together to fabricate a charge against him; they say his ordainer handed over the holy books. Thus they broke the nets of peace and now wander through the sea.

All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly. Behold how good and pleasant it is for brothers to dwell in unity! (Psalm 133:1). Hear the voice of the prophet, so that you may be in unity. Who proved to you the ancient charge of handing over? Who brought it forward in judgment? Those who sat to judge? By what witnesses was he convicted? Who dared to affirm it? But they gladly invented what they knew they themselves had done. Because rumor was already speaking about the handing over of the books, but those who had done it were hiding in that disturbance, so they defamed others so that they could hide themselves. Through them the rest went astray, the leaders from that party, because they thought it shameful not to believe their colleagues. Now, brothers, let the error end and let us be in unity.

All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly. They did what they wanted then in that blindness. Judges did not sit, priests did not sit according to custom, as they usually do when gathered to judge in great cases. Accuser and defendant did not stand in examination; there was no witness, no document by which they could prove the charge. But fury, deceit, and tumult, which reign in falsehood. Let the records be brought forward to us, the kind that are usually made in a council; let us see what thing compelled the making of altar against altar. If the priest was evil, he should have been deposed first; if he could not be deposed, he should have been tolerated within the net, just as you now tolerate so many openly evil men, and you who bear them with pious fury would have borne one for peace.

All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly. It would be a great joy for us if you had refused to go astray then; but if the truth was not seen then, now at least see it from experience. You now have many wicked men who displease you greatly, and yet you do not separate them from your communion. I am not speaking of those sins which you can deny: I speak of clubs, fires, deaths, which your people commit in the light, and yet you tolerate them either by error or by fear. How much was it for your fathers to bear one for unity, if the tumult was so great that they could not depose him? Add that he was innocent and they could prove nothing. But so that the charge would not be investigated, where they saw themselves to be, they pretended to be exceedingly righteous, when they wanted to throw everything into confusion.

All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly. Whoever seeks empty honors does not want to reign with Christ, like the prince of this evil, from whom their party is named. For Donatus then wanted to obtain all Africa; then he sought overseas judges from the emperor. But this so-just petition was not from love. The truth itself cries this out, which I want now to relate. For the emperor consented and sent priests to sit in Rome who could then hear Caecilian with him. The case was heard, nothing was proven: he dared even to appeal, and after the see of his colleagues to be heard by the emperor. By this that petition is proven not to be from love. Then, defeated everywhere, he began to rebaptize Christians.

All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly. If you want to follow justice, consider the whole case. What Donatus did afterward, why was it not done before? The priests were in disagreement throughout the whole African region: overseas priests could judge about it. Why did you run to schism and altar against altar, so that what was afterward judged you could no longer hear, and you were compelled by your own judges to appeal, while you want to confirm the reign of error in any way? And now you all know the whole matter, but you pretend not to know, and when the truth presses you, you say your fathers went astray, as if someone forbids you now to withdraw from error. But pride has bound you in the seat of pestilence.

All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly. Whoever has the love of Christ cannot hate peace. Listen now, you peoples, and agree with us—you who do not hold the see for which you fight unjustly. If your bishops from some one region had a dispute among themselves, whom would you want to judge it except bishops of other regions who were not part of that dispute? But when they had examined the case, they would pronounce for one side; you would never communicate with those who refused to agree with them. Why then did you communicate with these men, who did this before? For they too did not agree with the sentence of the overseas bishops, who judged for us; for they are joined to us today. If Christ the judge should say this, what do you have to answer? All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly.

If the light of the heart is in you, you can see the truth. There are the prayers and the records of Donatus, by which you prove what has been said. If you do not want to believe these, bring forward some of your own. If we do not believe those either, there will be a quarrel without end. Let us embrace peace, then. What is it to us what was done before? You throw the betrayal at us: we answer that you did it. You cry out about Macarius: and we about the circumcellion. That matter of ours is now past: yours do not cease even today. Our threshing floor has chaff: you want it to be only this; for you do not want peace. Those men threaten with the club: and if only they threatened and did not beat people daily. If these men of yours expel them, they have no one through whom to reign. All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly.

If Macarius exceeded the measure written in Christian law, or he was citing the law of the king, so that he might fight for unity. I do not say that he sinned nothing, but that yours are worse. For who commanded them to rage like this through Africa? It is proven that neither Christ nor the emperor permitted this—private clubs and fires and madness without law. Because it is written, “Put your sword back into its place” (Matthew 26:52), they do not think it a crime with a club—not that a man should die, but that he should be beaten severely and afterward die from it, already tortured by weakness. But even so, if they pity, they kill with even one club. They call the clubs “Israels,” which they said with honor, so that they may lay waste the name itself more than the body they strike with it. All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly.

Do not now, brothers, charge the time of Macarius to us. If those men were cruel, they displease us greatly too; but if they speak falsely about them, God can judge. Let us love the peace of Christ, let us rejoice in unity. If there are evil men in the church, they can do us no harm. If they cannot be with us, let them be excluded with peace preserved. If they cannot be excluded, let them at least be excluded from the heart. Holy Ezekiel said that certain ones were marked, who groan over the sins of their brothers and do not separate themselves from them. So let us not separate ourselves from our mother because of evil brothers, as the impious did then, raising an altar outside, so that they now have worse men than those they pretend to have fled. All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly.

Everyone who reads the scriptures knows what I want to reveal. John the Baptist said openly to the Jews then, that Christ could winnow them like his threshing floor. He sent workers into the harvest, his disciples, to preach, through whom the threshing floor was gathered and winnowed from the cross. Then the righteous, like wheat, filled the churches purely, selling what they possessed and saying farewell to the world. They were like seed that was scattered through the whole world, so that another harvest might rise, which is to be winnowed at the end. This grows among the weeds, because there are heresies everywhere; its chaff is the unjust, who are not in unity. If Macarius was from among these, why do you want to rebaptize us? All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly.

Set two threshing floors in your heart, so that you can see what I am saying. Certainly the earlier ones also had holy men, as the scriptures show. For God said he had left himself seven thousand men (1 Kings 19:18), and many priests and kings are righteous in the law. There you have so many prophets, and you have many from the people too. Tell me which of the righteous then separated an altar for himself. That wicked people committed many crimes: sacrifice was made to idols, so many prophets were killed, and yet none of the righteous withdrew from unity. The righteous endured the unjust until the coming winnower; they were mixed in one temple, but they were not mixed in heart. They said such things against them, and they had one altar. All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly.

What does this seem like to you? The second harvest of the church, which grows through the whole world, ought to endure more. It has also the Lord’s example in Judas the traitor. He bore with him among the good; he sent him also to preach. The evil servant preached, but Christ was in the faith, because those who believed the judge did not care about the herald. When he gave the holy supper, he did not exclude him from it even then, and he could have been betrayed by him even if he had gone out before. But an example was given to us to tolerate evil brothers, so that when they cannot be excluded, we are separated only in heart. All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly.

I ask you, answer us: why do you want to rebaptize? You drive your fallen priests from communion, and yet no one after them has dared to rebaptize, and all whom they baptized communicate with you today. What did they receive from them, if they did not have anything to give? Read how adulterers are punished in the holy law; for they cannot say that they sinned from fear. If only the holy baptize, rebaptize after these men. Why do you accuse us falsely, because we are in unity—we who were not yet born in that persecution? It is written that the sins of the fathers do not belong to the sons, but no one gives good fruit if he is cut off from the vine. All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly.

You know what the catholic is and what is cut off from the vine. If there are any cautious ones among you, let them come and live in the root; before they dry up too much, let them now be freed from the fire. Therefore we do not rebaptize, because there is one sign in the faith—not because we see you as holy, but because you hold only the form, because the branch that is cut off from the vine has the form itself. But what does the form profit it, if it does not live from the root?

Come, brothers, if you wish, so that you may be grafted into the vine. It is painful when we see you cut off and lying there like that. Count the bishops even from the very see of Peter, and look at that line of fathers: see who succeeded whom. That is the rock which the proud gates of the underworld do not overcome. All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly.

Suppose someone like this comes to you full of catholic faith—the kind of holy men we are all accustomed to hear about—and says to you: "Brother, why do you wish to rebaptize me? I do not know what happened before, but now I am in the faith of Christ. If what I do not know stains me, then show me what you yourself are like now. Look, I am watching your face, but I do not know what is in your heart. If what I do not know stains me, then perhaps you stain me—and if I believe you are holy, look at those with whom you share communion. If what I do not know stains, then you can no longer be holy, since so many sins stain you, which your people commit in secret. But if you do not care about what you do not know, then neither do I care about what happened before." And yet you dare to rebaptize such a Christian.

All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly. Woe to you who contend so unjustly for your sees. You shout that you alone are holy, but you say something else in your heart, because you see that many evil people abound everywhere among you too. Can you say, "We are mixed within the net"? The answer comes back to you: you have already broken it. Nor can you say that you endure the chaff; again we answer: you would have done this before too. For they were not worse than that traitor Judas, with whom the apostles received the first sacrament of the supper, when they already knew that the man guilty of so great a crime was among them. Yet the filth in another's heart did not stain them. And still you dare to rebaptize Christian brothers.

All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly. Hear what I say, brothers, and do not be angry with me. Because what you hear is not false—you can also consider it for yourselves. What if mother Church herself were to address you with peace and say: "O my children, why do you complain about your mother? Why have you deserted me? I want to hear it from you now. You accuse your brothers, and I am torn apart greatly. When the nations pressed me down, I endured many things with sorrow. Many deserted me, but they did so in fear. But no one forced you to rebel against me like this. You say you are with me, but you see that it is false: I am called catholic, and you are of Donatus's party. The apostle commanded me to pray for the kings of the world; you are envious that kings are now in the Christian faith. If you are children, why are you envious that my prayers have been heard? For when they sent gifts, you refused to accept them, and you forgot the prophets who foretold this before—that the great kings of the nations would send gifts to the church. When you rejected those gifts, you showed that you were not my children, and you forced Macarius to avenge his own grief. But what have I done to you, your mother throughout the whole world? I expel the evil ones I can; those I cannot, I am forced to bear. I bear them until they are healed or separated at the end. Why have you abandoned me, and why am I tormented by your death? If you hate evil people so much, look at what kind you have among yourselves. If you too tolerate evil people, why not in unity, where no one rebaptizes and there is no altar against altar? You tolerate so many evil people, but with no good reward, because what you ought to bear for Christ, you wish to bear for Donatus."
We have sung to you, brothers, of peace, if you wish to hear. Our judge is coming: we give, he demands.

problems.quote: What persecution did not do, they themselves did in peace.
problems.source_quote: quod persecutio non fecit, ipsi fecerunt in pace.
problems.why: English inverts meaning: source says persecution didn't cause schism, they did it in peacetime; English implies persecution failed where they succeeded.
problems.fix: What persecution never did, they did in time of peace.

problems.quote: If what we do not know stains, then you can no longer be holy
problems.source_quote: si maculat quod nescimus, iam non potes sanctus esse
problems.why: English 'we' for 'nescimus' is wrong; source has 'what I do not know' (singular, continuing the hypothetical catholic's speech).
problems.fix: If what I do not know stains, then you can no longer be holy
problems.ruling: 'nescimus' is first-person singular; the speaker says 'what I do not know.' English 'we' misattributes the speaker's voice.

problems.quote: But what have I done to you, your mother throughout the whole world?
problems.source_quote: sed ego quid uobis feci, uestra mater in toto orbe?
problems.why: English makes 'your mother' apposition to 'I'; source is vocative address: 'But I, what have I done to you? O your mother throughout the whole world...'
problems.fix: But what have I done to you? I, your mother throughout the whole world
problems.ruling: 'uestra mater' is vocative; English apposition 'your mother' to 'I' misreads the syntax and address structure.

problems.quote: he was citing the law of the king, so that it might fight for unity
problems.source_quote: uel legem regis referebat, ut pugnaret pro unitate
problems.why: "uel" means "or" (alternative), not "he was"—the line offers two possibilities: either Macarius exceeded the measure, OR he was citing the king's law so that *he* (Macarius) might fight for unity.
problems.fix: or he was citing the law of the king, so that he might fight for unity

problems.quote: They call the clubs "Israels," which they said with honor
problems.source_quote: fustes Israheles uocant, quod dixerunt cum honore
problems.why: "quod" refers to the naming, not "which they said"—"which they spoke with honor" or "a name they gave with honor"; more critically, "Israheles" is nominative plural or genitive singular, likely "Israels" as a name they call the clubs, but "quod" suggests "which (name) they spoke with honor."
problems.fix: They call the clubs "Israels," a name they spoke with honor

problems.quote: I, your mother throughout the whole world I expel the evil ones I can
problems.source_quote: sed ego quid uobis feci, uestra mater in toto orbe? expello malos quos possum
problems.why: The English merges two sentences awkwardly, losing the rhetorical question "But what have I done to you?"—the repetition of "I" creates confusion about whether "I expel" continues the question or starts a new statement.
problems.fix: But what have I done to you, your mother throughout the whole world? I expel the evil ones I can

problems.quote: But this seemingly just petition was not from love.
problems.source_quote: sed haec tam iusta petitio non erat de caritate
problems.why: "tam" means "so" or "this" (demonstrative), not "seemingly"—the petition *was* just, not seemingly just.
problems.fix: But this so-just petition was not from love.
problems.ruling: "tam iusta" means "so just"; "seemingly" wrongly implies the petition was not actually just.

problems.quote: It is not proven that Christ or the emperor permitted this
problems.source_quote: non Christus, non imperator haec probatur permisisse
problems.why: "probatur" governs the whole: "It is proven that neither Christ nor the emperor permitted this"—the double "non" is emphatic negation, not "not proven."
problems.fix: It is proven that neither Christ nor the emperor permitted this
problems.ruling: "probatur" means "it is proven"; English "not proven" reverses the source meaning.

problems.quote: But still, if they have mercy, they kill with one club
problems.source_quote: sed tamen si miserentur, occidunt et uno fuste
problems.why: "et" here means "even"—"they kill even with one club" (i.e., even a single blow kills), not "if they have mercy, they kill with one club" which makes no sense of "si miserentur."
problems.fix: But even so, if they pity, they kill with even one club
problems.ruling: "et" means "even"; "if they have mercy, they kill" is self-contradictory and misleads readers.

problems.quote: What persecution never did, they did in time of peace.
problems.source_quote: quod persecutio non fecit, ipsi fecerunt in pace.
problems.why: "never" is not in source; "non fecit" means "did not do," not "never did."
problems.fix: What persecution did not do, they did in time of peace.

problems.quote: They say they believed their own people: I say they lied.
problems.source_quote: suis se dicunt credidisse: dico ego mentitos esse;
problems.why: Source says "I say they lied" (past tense, about belief in their own), not "they lied" as ongoing claim.
problems.fix: They say they believed their own: I say they have lied.

problems.quote: The case was finished long ago, because you do not stand in peace.
problems.source_quote: olim iam causa finita est, quod uos non statis in pace.
problems.why: "quod" = "that/as for the fact that," not "because"; wrong causal logic.
problems.fix: The case was finished long ago; as for you, you do not stand in peace.

problems.quote: If the light of the heart is in you, you can see the truth.
problems.source_quote: Lumen cordis si est in uobis, uerum potestis uidere.
problems.why: "Lumen cordis" = light of the heart (subjective genitive), not "light...in you" as external.
problems.fix: If the light of heart is in you, you can see the truth.

problems.quote: Who brought it forward in judgment? Who sat to judge?
problems.source_quote: quis obiecit in iudicio? qui sederunt iudicare?
problems.why: 'qui sederunt iudicare' = 'those who sat to judge' (relative clause), not a question 'Who sat to judge?'. The English makes it a separate question, changing the syntax and sense.
problems.fix: Who brought it forward in judgment? Those who sat to judge?
problems.ruling: Latin 'qui' is relative 'those who,' not interrogative 'who?'; syntax misrepresented.

problems.quote: Because we also believed our own people, who say they handed over.
problems.source_quote: quia et nos credidimus nostris, qui eos dicunt tradidisse.
problems.why: "nostris" = our own people, not "who say they handed over" but "who say that they [the others] handed over."
problems.fix: For we too believed our own, who say that they handed them over.
problems.ruling: qui eos dicunt tradidisse: 'who say that they [the traditores] handed over'; English implies their own people handed over.

fixed: What persecution never did: source 'quod persecutio non fecit' means 'what persecution did not do'; 'never' is not in the source.
They say they believed their own people: source 'dico ego mentitos esse' is perfect infinitive, so 'I say they have lied' better reflects the past tense.
The case was finished long ago: source 'quod uos non statis in pace' uses 'quod' as 'as for the fact that', not causal 'because'.
Who brought it forward in judgment: source 'qui sederunt iudicare' is a relative clause ('those who sat to judge'), not a separate question.
Because we also believed our own people: source 'qui eos dicunt tradidisse' means 'who say that they handed them over', not 'who say they handed over'.

fixed.quote: He carried him among the good; he sent him also to preach
fixed.fix: He bore with him among the good; he sent him also to preach
fixed.note: Ferebat here means 'tolerated', which is the stanza's point (malos fratres tolerare); 'carried' misleads, and 'bore him' is awkward.

fixed.quote: But what have I done to you? But what have I done to you, your mother throughout the whole world?
fixed.fix: But what have I done to you, your mother throughout the whole world?
fixed.note: The English repeats the question; the source has it once.

dismissed.quote: They could excuse the matter of the books out of fear, because Peter denied Christ when he was terrified of death.
dismissed.why: 'qui' = 'who could excuse' is relative, not independent; 'modo quo pacto' = 'now how' is omitted.
dismissed.note: The English keeps both the sense and 'now how will they excuse'; splitting the relative clause into a separate sentence is a fair choice.

dismissed.quote: The case was finished long ago; as for you, you do not stand in peace.
dismissed.why: 'quod' = 'because' (causal), not 'as for you'; the causal link is lost.
dismissed.note: Here quod means 'as for the fact that'; a causal 'because' would make no sense, so the English is a fair rendering.

dismissed.quote: the vessels are the seats of the saints, where they cannot arrive
dismissed.why: "quo" refers to the sea (mare), not the vessels; the wicked cannot reach the saints' seats
dismissed.note: 'They' correctly refers back to those who broke the nets, and the proposed fix wrongly makes 'the sea' the subject.
